claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys are primarily governed by the interplay between chemical ordering and grain-boundary density.
The baseline as-deposited alloy has an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The baseline as-deposited alloy has relatively large grains.
Reducing deposition temperature or applying rapid cooling will refine the alloy microstructure.
Microstructural refinement will produce a higher density of grain boundaries.
Reducing deposition temperature or applying rapid cooling will modestly suppress long-range chemical ordering.
Grain boundaries in the refined microstructure provide additional nucleation sites for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
The additional grain-boundary nucleation sites lower the energy barrier for the magnetostructural transition.
Lowering the transition barrier broadens the temperature range of the magnetostructural transition.
Lowering the transition barrier reduces hysteretic energy loss.
The refined state is expected to have a slightly lower peak magnetic entropy change than the baseline.
The refined microstructure will enable faster heat exchange because of an increased surface-to-volume ratio.
Lower-deposition-temperature samples will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric transition than the baseline.
Lower-deposition-temperature samples will exhibit less hysteresis than the baseline.
Lower-deposition-temperature samples will exhibit improved heat transfer relative to the baseline.
The magnetocaloric transition will become more reversible under low-field cycling after the intervention.
The predictions are expected to hold within the studied non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi system under low-field magnetic-cooling cycles when composition, cost, and mechanical stability are held constant.
